recheck.why: Lint is 1.000 and clean (`skills\dv-formal-convergence\SKILL.md [approve 1.000] clean; 1/1 clean, 0 errors, 0 advisories`). Q2 budget arithmetic balances exactly: 3 Globs (report s1, property source s2 reused by s5/s6, filelist s4), 4 Greps (status strings s1, assertion/cover labels s2, hard-structure names s4, property label s5), 6 Reads (80 s3, 40+30 s4, 40+40 s5, 40 spare s6); steps 7-9 open nothing. Q4 all nine local slots plus the two profile facts (Filelist convention, Sign-off) are consumed. Q5 every block field has an assigning step, and `proof status` copies the registered T1 enum verbatim with all six tokens (so no T2 narrowing row is owed, consistent with dv-formal-apps and dv-formal-overconstraint-credit which correctly carry theirs); `notes` is last, no `signature` field, `run id` spelling matches the T3 shape lock and its usage matches the siblings. Q6 role/level are exactly formal-verification/senior; review-by 2027-04-23 is ~8.6 months out and unique in the pack. Q3 nothing proprietary is asserted — result strings, engine names, bound semantics and start-state support are all deferred to slots or to a named handoff. Q1 fails: step 7's ledger labels `bound-the-property` as `stronger-property` with no qualifier, and that inverts for an antecedent-side unbounded delay, which is exactly the property shape a convergence skill sees. Q8 no — a wrong soundness direction in the one table the skill exists to get right is the failure named in its own first paragraph. Length is 385 lines against the stated 180-260, but every sibling runs 359-442, so that is the pack norm and I am not counting it.
remaining: Step 7 ledger, row `| bound-the-property | stronger-property | a proof implies the original | a counterexample need not be one for the original claim |` is unqualified and inverts when the unbounded range sits in the ANTECEDENT. For `req ##[1:$] ack |-> ##[1:3] done` bounded to `req ##[1:8] ack |-> ##[1:3] done`, the bounded property matches fewer antecedents and is therefore WEAKER: a proof does not imply the original (acks at cycle 9+ are left unchecked) and a counterexample to the bounded form IS a counterexample to the original. Both the 'Survives the change' and 'What it can make wrong' cells are backwards for that case. Every other flippable row in the same table carries its qualifier in the first cell (`counter-abstraction, terminal count left free`; `start-state, from a state the reset sequence provably reaches`; `case-split with a proven-exhaustive guard set`; helper-lemma split into two rows) — this row needs the same treatment, i.e. a consequent/obligation-side row (stronger-property) and an antecedent-side row (weaker; neither result transfers without an argument).

Step 5's detection bullet 'an unbounded range (`##[1:$]`), `s_eventually`, or a strong operator — a liveness obligation' mislabels antecedent-side `##[1:$]`, which is a thread-explosion complexity problem, not a liveness obligation. That mislabel feeds step 6 row `| Liveness, or an unbounded range in the property | property-shape | bound-the-property |` and then the wrong step 7 row. Fix all three together or the chain stays inconsistent.

The Human verification section enumerates the soundness inversions to check ('a `blackbox` written as `soundness: under-approximation` is backwards'; '`constrain-environment` and `start-state` both restrict the model and are therefore `soundness: under-approximation`') but has no bullet for the bound-the-property direction, which is the one this recheck found wrong. Add it once the ledger is split.

Step 6's 'The spare 40-line **Read** goes wherever the chosen row points — the counter declaration, the array, or the parameter' has no anchor inside the stated budget. All 3 Globs and all 4 Greps are spent, and step 4's Grep is anchored to `crc`, `lfsr`, `scramble`, `ecc`, `syndrome`, `galois` plus wide multiply/divide — it never locates a counter, an array or a parameter declaration, and step 4's filelist Read yields directories rather than files. So for `counter-abstraction`, `parameter-shrink` and `symbolic-constant on one entry` there is no way to place that Read, and `edit : <the exact change and the file it belongs in>` becomes a guess for three of the twelve techniques. Either widen step 4's Grep alternation to carry the counter/array/parameter cues (still one Grep), or make the spare Read explicitly conditional and route the unanchored cases to a handoff.

Step 4's 'spend the 30-line **Read** on it to turn it into a short list of source directories' cannot follow a nested filelist, and the profile row it cites explicitly anticipates nesting ('how our filelists nest and include'). A 30-line window on an entry point of `-f` includes returns sub-filelist paths, not source directories. The escape hatch that follows is conditioned only on the row being unfilled or the filelist being invisible, not on it being nested — extend it to cover 'the entry point is a list of includes' and send that to the same handoff.

Minor, would not block alone: the budget describes step 5's Grep as covering 'that one property's label and its assumption set' but step 5 only Greps the label ('**Grep** the one property's label to get line numbers'), leaving the second 40-line assumption-set window with no stated way to be placed. Make the step's Grep an alternation over the label and the assumption keyword so the step and the budget agree.

Minor, would not block alone: step 6 asserts 'Every cell in the right-hand column is one of the `technique` tokens step 9's block accepts, spelled the way the block spells it', but several cells carry prose beside the token — `bound-the-property (counter-abstraction next iteration)`, `blackbox — only if the property does not check its value`, `none — go back to step 5 and check vacuity` — and the array row's cell contains the word `blackbox` as a negation ('symbolic-constant on one entry, **not** a blackbox'), which an agent copying 'the cell' could misread.
